sanskrit: eṣāṃ dvaidhaṃ samutpannaṃ yodhānāṃ yudhi bhārata tejovadho naḥ kriyate pratyakṣeṇa viśeṣataḥ
english: A division has arisen among these warriors on the eve of battle, O Bhārata, and our ardor is being plainly and grievously sapped.

sanskrit: rathānāṃ kva ca vijñānaṃ kva ca bhīṣmo 'lpacetanaḥ aham āvārayiṣyāmi pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: What does Bhīṣma, dull of wit, know of the reckoning of chariot-warriors? I myself will hold back the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: āsādya mām amogheṣuṃ gamiṣyanti diśo daśa pāṇḍavāḥ sahapañcālāḥ śārdūlaṃ vṛṣabhā iva
english: Coming upon me, whose arrows never miss, the Pāṇḍavas with their Pāñcālas will scatter to the ten directions as bulls flee before a tiger.

sanskrit: kva ca yuddhavimardo vā mantrāḥ suvyāhṛtāni vā kva ca bhīṣmo gatavayā mandātmā kālamohitaḥ
english: What has the clash of battle, or counsels well spoken, to do with Bhīṣma, his vigor spent, feeble in spirit, befuddled by age?

sanskrit: spardhate hi sadā nityaṃ sarveṇa jagatā saha na cānyaṃ puruṣaṃ kaṃ cin manyate moghadarśanaḥ
english: For he is forever contending with the whole world, and in his vain conceit he esteems no other man at all.

sanskrit: śrotavyaṃ khalu vṛddhānām iti śāstranidarśanam na tv evāpy ativṛddhānāṃ punar bālā hi te matāḥ
english: "The aged are indeed to be heeded"—so the scriptures teach; yet not the overaged, for such are reckoned children once more.

sanskrit: aham eko haniṣyāmi pāṇḍavān nātra saṃśayaḥ suyuddhe rājaśārdūla yaśo bhīṣmaṃ gamiṣyati
english: I alone shall slay the Pāṇḍavas, of this there is no doubt; yet in a well-fought battle, O tiger among kings, the glory will fall to Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: kṛtaḥ senāpatis tv eṣa tvayā bhīṣmo narādhipa senāpatiṃ guṇo gantā na tu yodhān kathaṃ cana
english: You have made this Bhīṣma your commander, O lord of men; the honor will go to the commander, never in any way to the fighters.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ jīvati gāṅgeye yotsye rājan kathaṃ cana hate tu bhīṣme yodhāsmi sarvair eva mahārathaiḥ
english: While the son of Gaṅgā lives, O king, I will by no means fight; but once Bhīṣma is slain, I shall do battle against all the great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca samudyato 'yaṃ bhāro me sumahān sāgaropamaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrasya saṃgrāme varṣapūgābhicintitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: This burden of mine that I take up is mighty, vast as the sea—the war of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, brooded upon for years on end.

sanskrit: tasminn abhyāgate kāle pratapte lomaharṣaṇe mithobhedo na me kāryas tena jīvasi sūtaja
english: Now that the hour has come, scorching and hair-raising, I must work no discord among us—and it is for that you live, O son of a sūta.

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ nādya vikramya sthaviro 'pi śiśos tava yuddhaśraddhāṃ raṇe chindyāṃ jīvitasya ca sūtaja
english: For old as I am, were I to put forth my strength this day, I could in battle cut short both your appetite for war and your very life, O son of a sūta.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa mahāstrāṇi pramuñcatā na me vyathābhavat kā cit tvaṃ tu me kiṃ kariṣyasi
english: When Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, loosed his great weapons against me, not a tremor touched me—and what then will you do to me?

sanskrit: kāmaṃ naitat praśaṃsanti santo ''tmabalasaṃstavam vakṣyāmi tu tvāṃ saṃtapto nihīna kulapāṃsana
english: The good, to be sure, do not praise this vaunting of one's own might; yet, stung as I am, I will speak to you, base wretch, blot upon your line.

sanskrit: sametaṃ pārthivaṃ kṣatraṃ kāśirājñaḥ svayaṃvare nirjityaikarathenaiva yat kanyās tarasā hṛtāḥ
english: At the bride-choice of the king of Kāśi, with but a single chariot I overcame the whole assembled warrior nobility and carried off the maidens by main force.

sanskrit: īdṛśānāṃ sahasrāṇi viśiṣṭānām atho punaḥ mayaikena nirastāni sasainyāni raṇājire
english: Thousands of such men, and of finer ones besides, were swept aside by me alone, together with their armies, upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: tvāṃ prāpya vairapuruṣaṃ kurūṇām anayo mahān upasthito vināśāya yatasva puruṣo bhava
english: With you for their man of strife a great calamity has come upon the Kurus, for their destruction. Make your effort; prove yourself a man.

sanskrit: yudhyasva pārthaṃ samare yena vispardhase saha drakṣyāmi tvāṃ vinirmuktam asmād yuddhāt sudurmate
english: Fight Pārtha in battle, with whom you so vie—and I shall watch you come away unscathed from that combat, O most evil-minded one.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tam uvāca tato rājā dhārtarāṣṭro mahāmanāḥ mām avekṣasva gāṅgeya kāryaṃ hi mahad udyatam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the high-minded king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, spoke to him: Have regard for me, son of Gaṅgā, for a great task is upon us.

sanskrit: cintyatām idam evāgre mama niḥśreyasaṃ param ubhāv api bhavantau me mahat karma kariṣyataḥ
english: Let this above all be considered first—what is my highest good; for both of you, my lords, shall do great deeds for me.

sanskrit: bhūyaś ca śrotum icchāmi pareṣāṃ rathasattamān ye caivātirathās tatra tathaiva rathayūthapāḥ
english: And further I wish to hear of the foremost chariot-warriors among the foe, and who among them are atirathas, and likewise the leaders of chariot-bands.

sanskrit: balābalam amitrāṇāṃ śrotum icchāmi kaurava prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ vai idaṃ yuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: I wish to hear the strength and weakness of my enemies, O Kaurava; for when night has brightened into dawn this war will begin.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ete rathās te saṃkhyātās tathaivātirathā nṛpa ya cāpy ardharathā rājan pāṇḍavānām ataḥ śṛṇu
english: Bhīṣma said: These chariot-warriors of yours have been numbered, O king, and likewise the atirathas; and now, O monarch, hear of the half-chariot warriors of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yadi kautūhalaṃ te 'dya pāṇḍavānāṃ bale nṛpa rathasaṃkhyāṃ mahābāho sahaibhir vasudhādhipaiḥ
english: If today you are eager, O king, to know the strength of the Pāṇḍavas—their tally of chariot-warriors, O mighty-armed one, together with these lords of the earth—

sanskrit: svayaṃ rājā rathodāraḥ pāṇḍavaḥ kuntinandanaḥ agnivat samare tāta cariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: The king himself, that noble chariot-warrior, the son of Pāṇḍu, the joy of Kuntī—he will range through the battle like fire, my child, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu rājendra ratho 'ṣṭaguṇasaṃmitaḥ nāgāyutabalo mānī tejasā na sa mānuṣaḥ
english: As for Bhīmasena, O lord of kings, he is reckoned a chariot-warrior eightfold over—proud, with the strength of ten thousand elephants; in his fierce energy he is no mere mortal.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau tu rathinau dvāv eva puruṣarṣabhau aśvināv iva rūpeṇa tejasā ca samanvitau
english: The two sons of Mādrī are both chariot-warriors, bulls among men, in beauty like the Aśvins and endowed with like splendor.

sanskrit: ete camūmukhagatāḥ smarantaḥ kleśam ātmanaḥ rudravat pracariṣyanti tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: Standing at the forefront of the host, remembering the wrongs done them, they will rage abroad like Rudra—of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: sarva eva mahātmānaḥ śālaskandhā ivodgatāḥ prādeśenādhikāḥ pumbhir anyais te ca pramāṇataḥ
english: All of them are great-souled, towering like śāla trunks, and in stature they exceed other men by a span's measure.

sanskrit: siṃhasaṃhananāḥ sarve pāṇḍuputrā mahābalāḥ caritabrahmacaryāś ca sarve cātitapasvinaḥ
english: Lion-framed are all the sons of Pāṇḍu, of mighty strength; all have kept the vow of chastity and all are men of surpassing austerity.

sanskrit: hrīmantaḥ puruṣavyāghrā vyāghrā iva balotkaṭāḥ jave prahāre saṃmarde sarva evātimānuṣāḥ sarve jitamahīpālā digjaye bharatarṣabha
english: Modest, tigers among men, fierce in strength like tigers; in speed, in the striking blow, and in the press of battle every one of them is more than human; all of them, O bull of the Bharatas, have subdued the kings of the earth in their conquest of the quarters.

sanskrit: na caiṣāṃ puruṣāḥ ke cid āyudhāni gadāḥ śarān viṣahanti sadā kartum adhijyāny api kaurava udyantuṃ vā gadāṃ gurvīṃ śarān vāpi prakarṣitum
english: And no men can ever match them in handling their weapons, maces, and arrows, O Kaurava—neither in stringing the bow, nor in lifting the heavy mace, nor in drawing the shaft to the head.

sanskrit: jave lakṣyasya haraṇe bhojye pāṃsuvikarṣaṇe bālair api bhavantas taiḥ sarva eva viśeṣitāḥ
english: In speed, in striking the mark, in eating, in flinging up the dust of sport—even as boys they outdid you all.

sanskrit: te te sainyaṃ samāsādya vyāghrā iva balotkaṭāḥ vidhvaṃsayiṣyanti raṇe mā sma taiḥ saha saṃgamaḥ
english: Falling upon your army like tigers raging in strength, they will lay it waste in battle—let there be no encounter with them!

sanskrit: ekaikaśas te saṃgrāme hanyuḥ sarvān mahīkṣitaḥ pratyakṣaṃ tava rājendra rājasūye yathābhavat
english: Each one of them, in battle, could slay all the lords of the earth—as you yourself saw, O king of kings, at the Rājasūya sacrifice.

sanskrit: draupadyāś ca parikleśaṃ dyūte ca paruṣā giraḥ te saṃsmarantaḥ saṃgrāme vicariṣyanti kālavat
english: Remembering the torment of Draupadī and the harsh words at the dicing, they will move through the battle like Death itself.

sanskrit: lohitākṣo guḍākeśo nārāyaṇasahāyavān ubhayoḥ senayor vīra ratho nāstīha tādṛśaḥ
english: Red-eyed, with hair drawn into a knot, and having Nārāyaṇa for his ally—in neither army, O hero, is there a chariot-warrior like that one.

sanskrit: na hi deveṣu vā pūrvaṃ dānaveṣūrageṣu vā rākṣaseṣv atha yakṣeṣu nareṣu kuta eva tu
english: For never of old, neither among gods nor Dānavas nor serpents, nor among Rākṣasas nor Yakṣas—still less among men—

sanskrit: bhūto 'tha vā bhaviṣyo vā rathaḥ kaś cin mayā śrutaḥ samāyukto mahārāja yathā pārthasya dhīmataḥ
english: have I heard of any chariot, past or yet to come, O great king, so equipped as that of the wise Pārtha.

sanskrit: vāsudevaś ca saṃyantā yoddhā caiva dhanaṃjayaḥ gāṇḍīvaṃ ca dhanur divyaṃ te cāśvā vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: Vāsudeva for his charioteer, and Dhanaṃjaya himself for the warrior; the Gāṇḍīva for his divine bow, and those horses swift as the wind;

sanskrit: abhedyaṃ kavacaṃ divyam akṣayyau ca maheṣudhī astragrāmaś ca māhendro raudraḥ kaubera eva ca
english: the impenetrable, divine armor, and the two inexhaustible great quivers; and the whole arsenal of weapons—those of Mahendra, of Rudra, and of Kubera;

sanskrit: yāmyaś ca vāruṇaś caiva gadāś cograpradarśanāḥ vajrādīni ca mukhyāni nānāpraharaṇāni vai
english: those of Yama and of Varuṇa, and maces dreadful to behold, and the chief weapons headed by the thunderbolt, missiles of every kind.

sanskrit: dānavānāṃ sahasrāṇi hiraṇyapuravāsinām hatāny ekarathenājau kas tasya sadṛśo rathaḥ
english: Thousands of Dānavas, dwellers in the City of Gold, were slain by that single chariot in battle—what chariot-warrior is the equal of him?

sanskrit: eṣa hanyād dhi saṃrambhī balavān satyavikramaḥ tava senāṃ mahābāhuḥ svāṃ caiva paripālayan
english: In his fury this mighty-armed one, strong and true in valor, would slay your army even while he guards his own.

sanskrit: ahaṃ cainaṃ pratyudiyām ācāryo vā dhanaṃjayam na tṛtīyo 'sti rājendra senayor ubhayor api ya enaṃ śaravarṣāṇi varṣantam udiyād rathī
english: I, or else the teacher, might go forth against this Dhanaṃjaya; there is no third in either army, O king of kings, who could advance upon him as he pours down his torrents of arrows.

sanskrit: jīmūta iva gharmānte mahāvātasamīritaḥ samāyuktas tu kaunteyo vāsudevasahāyavān taruṇaś ca kṛtī caiva jīrṇāv āvām ubhāv api
english: Like a storm-cloud at summer's end driven on by a great wind—so is the son of Kuntī when arrayed for war, with Vāsudeva for his ally; he is young and skilled, while we two are worn with age.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etac chrutvā tu bhīṣmasya rājñāṃ dadhvaṃsire tadā kāñcanāṅgadinaḥ pīnā bhujāś candanarūṣitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing this from Bhīṣma, the kings then felt their spirits sink, their stout arms ringed with golden armlets and smeared with sandal-paste.

sanskrit: manobhiḥ saha sāvegaiḥ saṃsmṛtya ca purātanam sāmarthyaṃ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ yathāpratyakṣadarśanāt
english: Their minds in turmoil, they recalled the prowess of the sons of Pāṇḍu of old, as though they beheld it before their very eyes.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca draupadeyā mahārāja sarve pañca mahārathāḥ vairāṭir uttaraś caiva ratho mama mahān mataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: The sons of Draupadī, O great king, are all five great chariot-warriors; and Uttara, the son of Virāṭa, I count a mighty chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: abhimanyur mahārāja rathayūthapayūthapaḥ samaḥ pārthena samare vāsudevena vā bhavet
english: Abhimanyu, O great king, is a chief among the leaders of chariot-bands; in battle he may prove the equal of Pārtha or of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: laghv astraś citrayodhī ca manasvī dṛḍhavikramaḥ saṃsmaran vai parikleśaṃ svapitur vikramiṣyati
english: Quick with his weapons, fighting with brilliant variety, spirited and firm in valor, he will show his prowess, remembering the wrongs done to his father.

sanskrit: sātyakir mādhavaḥ śūro rathayūthapayūthapaḥ eṣa vṛṣṇipravīrāṇām amarṣī jitasādhvasaḥ
english: Sātyaki of the Mādhava line, a hero, a chief among the leaders of chariot-bands—he, foremost of the Vṛṣṇi champions, is unforgiving and has conquered all fear.

sanskrit: uttamaujās tathā rājan ratho mama mahān mataḥ yudhāmanyuś ca vikrānto rathodāro nararṣabhaḥ
english: Uttamaujas too, O king, I count a mighty chariot-warrior; and Yudhāmanyu the valiant, a noble chariot-warrior, a bull among men.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ bahusāhasrā rathā nāgā hayās tathā yotsyante te tanuṃ tyaktvā kuntīputrapriyepsayā
english: These have many thousands of chariots, elephants, and horses; they will fight, casting away their lives out of love for the sons of Kuntī.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavaiḥ saha rājendra tava senāsu bhārata agnimārutavad rājann āhvayantaḥ parasparam
english: Together with the Pāṇḍavas, O king of kings, they will range through your armies, O Bhārata, like fire fanned by the wind, challenging one another.

sanskrit: ajeyau samare vṛddhau virāṭadrupadāv ubhau mahārathau mahāvīryau matau me puruṣarṣabhau
english: Unconquerable in battle though aged, both Virāṭa and Drupada—great chariot-warriors of mighty valor—I count as bulls among men.

sanskrit: vayovṛddhāv api tu tau kṣatradharmaparāyaṇau yatiṣyete paraṃ śaktyā sthitau vīragate pathi
english: Old in years though they are, devoted to the warrior's duty, they will strive to the utmost of their power, holding to the path that heroes tread.

sanskrit: saṃbandhakena rājendra tau tu vīryabalānvayāt āryavṛttau maheṣvāsau snehapāśasitāv ubhau
english: By their kinship, O king of kings, and through their lineage of valor and strength, these two great archers of noble conduct are both bound fast in the cords of affection.

sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ prāpya tu narāḥ sarva eva mahābhujāḥ śūrā vā kātarā vāpi bhavanti narapuṃgava
english: When a sufficient cause arises, O bull among men, all men of mighty arms become either heroes or cowards.

sanskrit: ekāyanagatāv etau pārthena dṛḍhabhaktikau tyaktvā prāṇān paraṃ śaktyā ghaṭitārau narādhipa
english: These two, made one in purpose with Pārtha and steadfast in devotion, will labor to the utmost of their power, O lord of men, casting away their very lives.

sanskrit: pṛthag akṣauhiṇībhyāṃ tāv ubhau saṃyati dāruṇau saṃbandhibhāvaṃ rakṣantau mahat karma kariṣyataḥ
english: Each at the head of an akṣauhiṇī, terrible in the fray, these two—guarding the bond of kinship—will do a great deed.

sanskrit: lokavīrau maheṣvāsau tyaktātmānau ca bhārata pratyayaṃ parirakṣantau mahat karma kariṣyataḥ
english: Heroes renowned in the world, great archers who have renounced all care for their lives, O Bhārata, guarding the trust placed in them, they will do a great deed.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca pāñcālarājasya suto rājan parapuraṃjayaḥ śikhaṇḍī rathamukhyo me mataḥ pārthasya bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: The son of the king of the Pāñcālas, O king, the conqueror of hostile cities, Śikhaṇḍin—him I count a foremost chariot-warrior on Pārtha's side, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: eṣa yotsyati saṃgrāme nāśayan pūrvasaṃsthitim paraṃ yaśo viprathayaṃs tava senāsu bhārata
english: He will fight in the battle, undoing what was settled of old, spreading his great fame abroad through your armies, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etasya bahulāḥ senāḥ pāñcālāś ca prabhadrakāḥ tenāsau rathavaṃśena mahat karma kariṣyati
english: Many are his hosts, the Pāñcālas and the Prabhadrakas; and with that array of chariots he will do a great deed.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca senānīḥ sarvasenāsu bhārata mato me 'tiratho rājan droṇaśiṣyo mahārathaḥ
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna, commander of all their forces, O Bhārata, I count an atiratha, O king—the pupil of Droṇa, a great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: eṣa yotsyati saṃgrāme sūdayan vai parān raṇe bhagavān iva saṃkruddhaḥ pinākī yugasaṃkṣaye
english: He will fight in the battle, cutting down the foe in combat, like the blessed Lord of the Pināka in his wrath at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: etasya tadrathānīkaṃ kathayanti raṇapriyāḥ bahutvāt sāgaraprakhyaṃ devānām iva saṃyuge
english: Of his army of chariots, those who delight in war say that, for its multitude, it is like the ocean, as in the battle-array of the gods.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmā tu rājendra mato me 'rdharatho nṛpa dhṛṣṭadyumnasya tanayo bālyān nātikṛtaśramaḥ
english: But Kṣatradharman, O king of kings, I count a half-chariot warrior, O monarch—the son of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, who by reason of his youth is not yet greatly seasoned.

sanskrit: śiśupālasuto vīraś cedirājo mahārathaḥ dhṛṣṭaketur maheṣvāsaḥ saṃbandhī pāṇḍavasya ha
english: The son of Śiśupāla, the heroic king of the Cedis, a great chariot-warrior and mighty archer—Dhṛṣṭaketu, a kinsman of the Pāṇḍava;

sanskrit: eṣa cedipatiḥ śūraḥ saha putreṇa bhārata mahārathenāsukaraṃ mahat karma kariṣyati
english: this valiant lord of the Cedis, together with his son, O Bhārata, a great chariot-warrior, will do a great and hard-wrought deed.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmarato mahyaṃ mataḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ kṣatradevas tu rājendra pāṇḍaveṣu rathottamaḥ jayantaś cāmitaujāś ca satyajic ca mahārathaḥ
english: Devoted to the warrior's duty, a conqueror of hostile cities, I count Kṣatradeva, O king of kings, a foremost chariot-warrior among the Pāṇḍavas; and Jayanta, and Amitaujas, and Satyajit the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: mahārathā mahātmānaḥ sarve pāñcālasattamāḥ yotsyante samare tāta saṃrabdhā iva kuñjarāḥ
english: Great chariot-warriors and great-souled, all the foremost of the Pāñcālas—they will fight in battle, my child, like elephants in fury.

sanskrit: ajo bhojaś ca vikrāntau pāṇḍaveṣu mahārathau pāṇḍavānāṃ sahāyārthe paraṃ śaktyā yatiṣyataḥ śīghrāstrau citrayoddhārau kṛtinau dṛḍhavikramau
english: Aja and Bhoja, both valiant, great chariot-warriors among the Pāṇḍavas, will strive to the utmost of their power in aid of the Pāṇḍavas—swift with their weapons, fighting with brilliant variety, skilled and firm in valor.

sanskrit: kekayāḥ pañca rājendra bhrātaro yuddhadurmadāḥ sarva ete rathodārāḥ sarve lohitakadhvajāḥ
english: The five Kekaya brothers, O king of kings, frenzied for battle—all of them noble chariot-warriors, all with crimson banners.

sanskrit: kāśikaḥ sukumāraś ca nīlo yaś cāparo nṛpaḥ sūryadattaś ca śaṅkhaś ca madirāśvaś ca nāmataḥ
english: The king of Kāśi, and Sukumāra, and Nīla, and that other king, and Sūryadatta, and Śaṅkha, and one named Madirāśva—

sanskrit: sarva ete rathodārāḥ sarve cāhavalakṣaṇāḥ sarvāstraviduṣaḥ sarve mahātmāno matā mama
english: all these are noble chariot-warriors, all bearing the marks of battle, all masters of every weapon, all great-souled—so I judge them.

sanskrit: vārdhakṣemir mahārāja ratho mama mahān mataḥ citrāyudhaś ca nṛpatir mato me rathasattamaḥ sa hi saṃgrāmaśobhī ca bhaktaś cāpi kirīṭinaḥ
english: Vārdhakṣemi, O great king, I count a mighty chariot-warrior; and king Citrāyudha I count a foremost chariot-warrior, for he is a splendor in battle and is devoted to the Diademed One.

sanskrit: cekitānaḥ satyadhṛtiḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathau dvāv imau puruṣavyāghrau rathodārau matau mama
english: Cekitāna and Satyadhṛti, two great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas—these two, tigers among men and noble chariot-warriors, so I judge them.

sanskrit: vyāghradattaś ca rājendra candrasenaś ca bhārata matau mama rathodārau pāṇḍavānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: And Vyāghradatta, O king of kings, and Candrasena, O Bhārata—both I count noble chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, beyond doubt.
